name: C Console Application
description: A small C program with a compile script and a run script you can edit, or CMake if you prefer. clangd works right away. No build system to learn: compile.sh builds every .c under src/.

options.label: Build system
options.hint: Scripts: plain compile.sh / run.sh you can read and change. CMake: the same scripts drive cmake for you.

win.hint: Scripts: plain compile.bat / run.bat you can read and change. CMake: the same scripts drive cmake for you.
msvc: Visual Studio's compiler (cl, found by compile.bat itself). gcc / clang: MinGW-w64 or LLVM on PATH.

options.label: Add a tests folder
options.hint: tests/test_main.c with plain assert(); run it with ./compile.sh test

win.hint: tests\test_main.c with plain assert(); run it with compile.bat test

options.label: Use ccache when installed
options.hint: ccache remembers what the compiler produced, so rebuilding code that did not change is nearly instant. Skipped automatically if ccache is not installed.

options.label: Use mold linker when installed
options.hint: mold is a very fast drop-in replacement for the system linker. It cuts the link step of larger programs from seconds to a blink. Skipped automatically if mold is not installed.

options.label: Add a .clang-format file
options.hint: Format Document uses it (LLVM style, 4 spaces).

win.description: A small C program with a compile script and a run script you can edit, or CMake if you prefer. clangd works right away. No build system to learn: compile.bat builds every .c under src\ with Visual Studio's compiler, MinGW or LLVM.
